graph.summary: Vancomycin → Lipid II → peptidoglycan biosynthetic process → Staphylococcus aureus

evidence.snippet: Vancomycin inhibits cell wall biosynthesis by targeting lipid II, which is the membrane-bound peptidoglycan precursor. The heptapeptide aglycon structure of vancomycin binds to the d-Ala-d-Ala of the pentapeptide stem structure in lipid II.
evidence.explanation: Vancomycin binds the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus of the peptidoglycan precursor lipid II.

paper.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Atomic Interactions in the Vancomycin Binding Site.

evidence.snippet: Vancomycin forms an intricate network of hydrogen bonds with the d-Ala-d-Ala region of Lipid II, interfering with the peptidoglycan layer maturation process.
evidence.explanation: Vancomycin binding to Lipid II interferes with peptidoglycan layer maturation (biosynthetic process).

paper.title: Molecular mechanisms of vancomycin resistance.
paper.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

evidence.snippet: Our results show the accumulation of peptidoglycan precursors after vancomycin treatment, consistent with transglycosylase inhibition
evidence.explanation: Inhibition of peptidoglycan biosynthesis (transglycosylase inhibition) leads to accumulation of precursors and impaired Staphylococcus aureus cell wall synthesis.

paper.title: Vancomycin and oritavancin have different modes of action in Enterococcus faecium.

evidence.snippet: Vancomycin is the first-line agent for MRSA in hospitalized patients
evidence.explanation: Vancomycin is the standard first-line treatment for MRSA infections in hospitalized patients.

paper.title: Skin and soft tissue infections in immunocompetent patients.
